claims.statement: Availability is limited by the protected-branches reusable to public Free and public/private Pro, Team or Enterprise plans. Version and redirect metadata do not adopt protection locally.
The source states that a required check must have completed successfully in the repository during the last seven days. This does not by itself establish success on the current merge SHA.
When a check run and commit status share a required name, BOTH must pass. A successful run alone cannot establish satisfaction.
Strict required checks require the branch to be updated from the base before merge, using merge or rebase.
The GH006 ci-build transcript illustrates a failed required check. It is not a local negative-test result or a prescribed check name.

If a pull request is up to date and required checks passed, the source permits local merging and pushing without checks on the merge commit itself. A policy requiring a separate integration-commit run is stricter local policy, not this universal platform requirement.

Only checks against the latest commit SHA satisfy requirements; checks against previous SHAs do not. GitHub accepts successful, skipped or neutral conclusions, so passing configuration is not proof that analysis executed.
When the test merge commit has a status check it must pass; otherwise the head commit check must pass. The displayed merge-branch indication helps distinguish the revision being checked.

GitHub Actions job checks must use eligible PR events (push, pull_request, pull_request_review, pull_request_target, deployment or deployment_status); workflow_dispatch success does not satisfy this PR ruleset check requirement. External App checks are exempt from this Actions-event limitation.
Queued Actions checks need merge_group as an additional event; it is separate from push and pull_request.
Skipping an entire workflow through path, branch or commit-message filters leaves associated checks Pending and can block a required-check pull request.
A job skipped by an if condition reports Success and does not block merge even when required. Success alone cannot prove work executed.

A job depending on a failed job can be skipped without reporting a failure and may not block merge. An always() condition with needs is recommended to ensure the dependent job reports; a safe aggregator must also examine dependency results.

The scripts/** example demonstrates workflow-level filtering that leaves a README-only PR waiting; its checkout/setup-node includes and Node-version matrix are source examples, not selected local dependencies or production versions.
The source requires adding merge_group to Actions required-check workflows for merge queues; the pull_request plus merge_group YAML is illustrative event configuration.
A required check restricted to an expected GitHub App must be produced by that App; a same-name check from another publisher does not meet the configured requirement.

scope: Full pinned article plus literal dependency reading; source evidence only, without adoption or live behavior verification.
